corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN (verdict unchanged). The nu-block construction is known from Marchetti et al. 2602.03655, Lemma B.8 Case 1 / eq. 71. The value nu^{-(nu-b)/b} B_p Gamma_{nu/b}(p), the budget-programme reduction, the frequency count, and the necessity of exactly nu equal neurons per frequency are not found in the ML literature. Fix to the recommended change: the b=nu recovery of Morwani Thm 7 and Li Thm 4.1 comes from thm:universal / cor:dense (power networks, C_b^{nu/b} = n! B_p), not from thm:cyclic.
issues: (1) The checker's recommended change is mathematically wrong. It says thm:cyclic at b=nu recovers Morwani Thm 7 and Li Thm 4.1, and the checker's rationale for citing Morwani says the same. thm:cyclic covers interference-free PRODUCT networks, whose value at b=nu is B_p p/(p-1). Morwani ((u+v)^2 w) and Li ((sum u_t)^k w, Def D.5) use POWER networks, whose values are n! times larger. Those values are recovered by thm:universal / cor:dense with C_b^{nu/b} = n! B_p. The paper already does this for Morwani (approach.tex:70, appendix.tex:32). I checked that n! B_p p/(p-1) equals Li's 2k!/((2k+2)^{(k+1)/2} p^{(k-1)/2}(p-1)) exactly (ratio 1.000 at p=7,11,113 and k=2,3,4), so that match can be added to cor:dense. The appendix itself says the nu-block does not attain the power bound (appendix.tex:266,279). (2) All five citations exist, and I checked each against the primary text. Marchetti: v2, 'Accepted at ICML 2026'; Lemma B.8 Case 1 quote and eq. 71 verbatim; Remark B.7 says 2^{k-1} Waring powers are optimal; sufficient construction only, no norm or necessity claim. Tian: Cor 2 (6 nodes per frequency, all frequencies), Cor 4 (order-4), Cor 5 (mixed 4/6), Thm 5 Occam's Razer, NeurIPS 2025. Gromov: Eq 12 and Eq 15 (approximate, random phases). Morwani: Thm 7. Li: Thm 4.1 (m >= 2^{2k-2}(p-1)). One nit in the checker's evidence: 'Corollaries 4 and 5: order-4 and mixed order-4/6' is right, but Cor 4 is specifically a single-frequency order-4 partial solution. (3) Minor: gromov2023grokking is in refs.bib but no section cites it, so the recommended sentence would be its first use. (4) The ML-lens search found no prior art for the theorem: arXiv listings for modular addition margin, grokking margin, grokking frequencies weight decay, and modular addition weight decay, plus Kunin et al. AGF 2506.06489 (cancellation by neuron pairs via the polarization identity, not a nu-block), Tian 2509.21519, Pracher et al. 2609.26679 (Sep 2026, NTK; no count or margin), and Tan-Gai-Zhang 2606.08985 (weight-decay surrogates favour a single-frequency rank-2 geometry, framed as a 'trade-off between separation, symmetry, and complexity'; relevant only to the title's framing, with no margin value or count law). (5) Why the workflow is slow, observed here: this session's WebSearch budget is exhausted (200/200, so every WebSearch call fails immediately); the arXiv export API returns HTTP 429 because parallel verifiers share one IP; the agents share a scratchpad directory, and another agent overwrote my marchetti.txt mid-run. Verifiers therefore fall back to slower WebFetch and PDF downloads.

extra_citations.why: Optional, for prior.tex framing only; not prior art for thm:cyclic. Argues that under weight-decay/Schatten surrogates modular addition prefers a single-frequency rank-2 cyclic geometry, governed by a 'trade-off between separation, symmetry, and complexity'. That overlaps the paper's 'margin-regularization trade-off' wording, so a reviewer may expect it discussed. It gives no max-margin value, no frequency-count law, and no nu-block.
